name: Lexicon LXP-1
source: Lexicon LXP-1 Owner's Manual, Part #070-06023, (c) 1988, Revision 1.2 (title page). Read directly, page images: freeverb3-vst.sourceforge.io/doc/Lexicon/lxp1.pdf (27 two-page spreads; this scan is missing pp.ii, 3-6/3-7 and 4-22) plus the 32-page scan bundled in github.com/evenbrenden/lxpx (owners_manuals/LXP-1_owners_manual.pdf, Rev 1.2, has the missing pages). Used: specifications p.vi (MIDI In + MIDI Thru, 5-pin DIN), front panel p.1-2 (INPUT/MIX/OUTPUT, 16-position Program selector, DECAY/DELAY, MIDI button + status LED), rear panel p.1-3 (MIDI THRU becomes OUT via an internal jumper), DEFEAT p.2-3, knob snap/LED blink p.2-4, programs + knob tables pp.2-5..2-10, MIDI channel / store / load registers pp.3-2..3-3, PC numbering p.3-4, Dynamic MIDI pp.3-4..3-7, MRC p.3-8, MIDI SysEx implementation ch.4 pp.4-1..4-22 (Active Setup 4-1, Stored 4-2, Packed Parameter Adjust + Requests 4-3, All Registers 4-4, Nibblized Parameter Adjust + Events 4-5, Transmitted + param classes 4-6..4-7, parameter map + patch sources + 16-bit ranges 4-8..4-9, 8/7 packing 4-9..4-10, per-algorithm tables 4-11..4-13, dump contents 4-14, common + specific params 4-15..4-22), MIDI implementation chart (last page). Cross-checks: evenbrenden/lxpx src/lxpx_helpers.c + lxpx.c (Pd external, 2012: F0 06 02 2n pp b0 b1 b2 F7, b0 = (bit15 << 1) | bit7, b1 = bits 0-6, b2 = bits 8-14, values clamped to 0x4000..0xBFFF; parameter_definitions.py: Delay 1 / Delay 2 param numbers + uni/bi); Opcode Galaxy 'Editor: Lexicon LXP-1/Reflex' tech pub (oldschooldaw.com/opcode/_TECHPUBS/LXP-1_Reflex.pdf: THRU->OUT jumper procedure, per-algorithm param lists matching pp.4-11..4-13, patch destination may be input level); monophreak.com 'Lexicon LXP-1 Internal Midi Jumper' (service manual: move jumper W3 -> W2 for OUT); Music Technology Dec 1988 review (muzines.co.uk, 16-position DECAY/DELAY knobs, 'as many as nine, none fewer than seven' hidden params); sysexdb.com/lexicon/lxp-1 (user note: F0 06 02 30 64 00 F7 'seems to work'). Edisyn and MidiQuest: no LXP-1 driver found. Electra One: only LXP-5/15 threads.

lexicon.statusByte: Byte 4 (1-based) = (type << 4) | n, n = MIDI channel 0-15 (the unit's one channel; no OMNI, Mode 3). type: 0 = Active Setup data, 1 = Stored (single register) data, 2 = Packed Parameter Adjust, 3 = Request, 4 = All Registers data, 5 = Nibblized Parameter Adjust, 6 = Event (pp.4-1..4-5).

formats.activeSetupData: F0 06 02 0n 38 <56 packed data bytes> <sumcheck> F7 = 63 bytes (p.4-1). 38h = packed byte count 56 (49 unpacked). The running edit buffer.
formats.packedParamAdjust: F0 06 02 2n <param 0-127> <b0> <b1> <b2> F7 = 9 bytes (p.4-3). The 16-bit value as a 2-byte partial packet: b0 = 0 0 0 0 0 hi7 lo7, b1 = lo bits 6-0, b2 = hi bits 6-0 (pp.4-9..4-10; lxpx helpers do exactly this). 'All parameter change messages require that a full 16 bits be sent': 8-bit params pad the hi byte with 0. Received value = new BASE value (overwrites the knob and vice versa, p.4-6). No reply.
formats.nibbleParamAdjust: F0 06 02 5n <param> <d3> <d2> <d1> <d0> F7 = 10 bytes (p.4-5): the 16-bit value as four nibbles, high nibble first. Equivalent alternative to 2n.
formats.request:
F0 06 02 3n

F7 = 7 bytes (p.4-3). e = 60h active setup, 61h one register (p = register 0-127), 62h packed param data (p = param #), 64h all registers, 65h nibble param data (p = param #). p must be present even when ignored. Replies use the receive formats A/B/C/E/F (p.4-6): 60h -> 0n dump, 61h -> 1n dump, 62h -> 2n param msg, 64h -> 4n dump, 65h -> 5n param msg (inferred pairing).
formats.allRegistersData: F0 06 02 4n 38 00 <7168 packed> <sumcheck> F7 = 7176 bytes (p.4-4). 38 00 = 7168 (0x1C00) as two 7-bit bytes, high first. 128 x 56 packed bytes, register 0 first, register 127 last (p.4-14). Each register is packed on its own (56 = 8 whole packets of 49/7 bytes).
formats.event: F0 06 02 6n <e> <reg 0-127> F7 = 7 bytes (p.4-5). 70h = store register (edit buffer -> register reg), 71h = recall register. No acknowledgement documented.
formats.packing: 8/7 packing (pp.4-9..4-10): every 7 unpacked 8-bit bytes a..g become 8 bytes: first a header 0 g7 f7 e7 d7 c7 b7 a7 (header bit i = msb of unpacked byte i), then a&7F .. g&7F. Least significant data first. A short final packet of k < 7 bytes sends a header with only k msbs, right-justified, then k bytes. The 49-byte dump is exactly 7 packets = 56 bytes.
formats.sumcheck: 'sumcheck of data bytes (sum done on the bytes in packed format)' (pp.4-1, 4-2, 4-4). Formula not given: candidates sum(packed) & 7F or (-sum(packed)) & 7F; whether the count byte(s) are included is not stated (assume not). Learn it from the first real dump.
formats.wordOrder: Inside the unpacked dump each 16-bit param takes 2 bytes (p.4-14) but their order is not printed. The parameter message puts the least-significant byte first (p.4-10), so assume lo, hi -- verify on the first dump.

lexicon.dumpLayout: 49 unpacked bytes (p.4-14): 0 = Program ID; 1-2 = param 0 (DECAY knob, 'RTime'); 3-4 = param 1 (DELAY knob, 'PDelay'); 5-20 = params 2-9 (2 bytes each; byte = 1 + 2 x param); 21-36 = name (params 32-47); 37-40 = patch sources (48-51); 41-44 = patch destinations (52-55); 45-48 = patch scales (56-59). Param 10 (input level), 60-63 (patch offsets), 64 (setup #) are not in the dump. Active setup and stored register have identical data.
lexicon.encoding: Microcode params 0-10 are 16-bit, centred on 0x8000 with a 0x3FFF span (pp.4-9, 4-10): unipolar 0x8000 (min) .. 0xBFFF (max); bipolar 0x4000 (most negative) .. 0x7FFF (least negative), 0x8000 = zero .. 0xBFFF (most positive). Out-of-range values are clamped by the unit. The resolution ('Num of Steps') is spread over the whole range, so the editor holds a step index s (0..steps-1) and maps uni: wire = 0x8000 + floor((s + 0.5) x 0x4000 / steps), read s = floor((wire - 0x8000) x steps / 0x4000); bi: wire = 0x4000 + floor((s + 0.5) x 0x8000 / steps), read s = floor((wire - 0x4000) x steps / 0x8000) (centre-of-bin; the unit's own quantisation is not documented). encoding 'lxp16uni' / 'lxp16bi'. 8-bit params (name 32-47, patches 48-59, setup 64, program ID 65) go in the low byte, hi byte 0; patch scales are 8-bit two's complement ('twos8').
lexicon.programNumbering: Setups (param 64): 0-127 = user registers 0-127 (Program Change n loads register n; register 0 = PC 0, p.3-4), 128-143 = ROM presets 0-15 = Program knob positions 0-15. The manual numbers registers from 0.
lexicon.transmits: Only with the internal jumper moved to MIDI OUT (factory: THRU; p.1-3, p.4-6). Then: replies to 3n requests; and a packed Parameter Adjust (2n) whenever a front-panel knob is turned -- param 0 for DECAY, 1 for DELAY, 64 (setup number) for the Program knob (p.4-6). The transmitted value is base + MIDI patch offset (p.4-8). Never transmits notes, CC, PC or clock (chart). Two LXP-1s can be slaved OUT -> IN.
lexicon.receives: Program Change 0-127 (loads register n), System Reset, SysEx (all formats above). Notes, note-on velocity, channel aftertouch, pitch bend, CC (chart 0-127; patch sources only 0-31 + 32 switches) and MIDI clock only as Dynamic MIDI patch sources. No OMNI.
lexicon.midiClock: Recognised only 'as controller': patch source 68 'MIDI tempo value'. No clock-synced delays are documented (unlike the LXP-5's tempo-synced delay patches).
lexicon.sharedWith: Not byte-compatible with the LXP-5 (model 05, raw 7-bit, one byte per param). Same Lexicon 06h framing and request/event codes (60h/61h/64h, 70h/71h). The Lexicon Reflex shares the register architecture (Opcode: same librarian module) -- its model byte and maps were not checked.

groups.name: Program: algorithm (Program ID 1-8) + effects level (param 2, every algorithm)
Dynamic MIDI patches 1-4: source, destination, scale
Live / system params (not stored): processor input level, setup number

params.name: Program ID (algorithm)
params.note: Byte 0 of every dump = program (algorithm) ID 1-8 (p.4-7 table, p.4-14). As a parameter it is #65, 8-bit, 'not stored during register save' (p.4-8) -- it is stored as dump byte 0 instead. Writing it 'controls which microcode algorithm is currently running' (p.4-7); every microcode param 0-9 changes meaning with it. 1 Rooms & Halls, 2 Plates, 3 Chorus 1 (stereo flange), 4 Delay 2 (4-tap bounce), 5 Chorus 2 (chromatic resonator), 6 Inverse, 7 Gate, 8 Delay 1 (6-voice chorus).

params.name: Effects Level
params.note: Param 2 in every algorithm (p.4-15 7A): final effects-processor output level before the MIX pot, 0-100%, 256 steps. Always 100% in the factory presets; meant for balancing registers against each other.

params.name: Rvb Mid Decay
params.range: 0.6-9 s typical (Bright Hall); per-preset ranges p.2-9
params.note: DECAY knob. 16 steps = the knob's 16 positions, so the knob reaches every value. RT60 range depends on the preset (Small 1 0.08-2.4 s .. Hall B 0.65-9.0 s, p.2-9); the step->seconds table is not published.

params.name: Pre-Delay
params.range: 0-262 ms via MIDI (0-8191 samples), 0-246 ms via knob
params.note: DELAY knob (16 positions, ms list p.2-6). Table p.4-11: 8192 steps; p.4-16 says 4096 steps of 2 samples via MIDI. ~32 us/step if 8192 steps over 262 ms.

params.name: Bass Multiply
params.note: Bipolar, 32 steps: wire 0x4000 = min (x0.3), 0x8000 = x1.0, 0xBFFF = max (x2.5) (p.4-11, p.4-16). Scales RT below 500 Hz. Shown centred: 0 = x1.0.

params.name: Hi Freq Cut
params.note: Param 4 per the Reverbs table (p.4-11); the Common Parameters page (p.4-15 7B) says '3 Reverbs', which collides with Bass Multiply -- see uncertain. 16 steps.

params.name: Size
params.note: Apparent room size, 8-71 m, 64 steps (p.4-17 8C). Size changes typically mute/glitch briefly (p.3-6 note).

params.name: Pre-Delay Feedback
params.note: Feedback around the pre-delay loop, -99..+99%, 512 steps (p.4-15 7C). Shown centred: 0 = no feedback.

params.name: Diffusion
params.note: Softens percussive attacks; 256 steps (p.4-16 7D).

params.name: Negative Feedback
params.note: DECAY knob. Ganged negative feedback around the flange; drives Right (3) and Left (6) Feedback and overrides any relation set between them (p.4-18 11A). Slightly more feedback on the left. Program table p.2-10: knob 0-94%.

params.name: Flange Depth
params.note: DELAY knob. Limit of flange notch travel, 0.25-8 ms (p.4-18 11B: 124 steps of 6.25 us; table p.4-11: 256 steps). Values <= 0x8200 (< 8 samples) are not installed (p.4-11 footnote).

params.name: Right Feedback
params.note: Independent feedback around right delay + flange (p.4-19 11D).

params.name: Right Delay
params.note: Independent predelay on the right flange (p.4-18 11C). Wire values above 0xBD00 are limited to 32000 samples = 1 s (p.4-12).

params.name: Shape
params.note: Flange sweep curve: more time in the high-frequency region. Factory 6 (p.4-19 11F).

params.name: Left Feedback
params.note: Independent feedback around left delay + flange (p.4-19 11D).

params.name: Left Delay
params.note: Independent predelay on the left flange (p.4-18 11C). The preset adds 'a slight amount of delay' on the left (p.2-7).

params.name: Rate
params.note: Sweep rate independent of depth. Table p.4-11: 16 steps; p.4-19 11E: '0 to 15, 32 steps, first major step from 0 to 1 subdivided into 16 minor steps' -- see uncertain.

params.name: Positive Feedback
params.note: DECAY knob: positive feedback around the longest tap, 0-94% (p.2-8). The full +-99% is the bipolar Feedback param 3.

params.name: Ganged Delay (tap spacing)
params.note: DELAY knob: first-tap time; the four taps are equally spaced, alternating L/R, exponential curve (p.2-8). Opcode's editor calls it 'Group Delay'.

params.name: Feedback
params.note: Bipolar feedback (p.4-12 table; +-99% via SysEx per p.2-8).

params.name: Left Delay
params.note: Table p.4-12, 256 steps. Time range not documented.

params.name: Right Delay
params.note: Table p.4-12, 256 steps. Time range not documented.

params.name: Hi Freq Cut
params.note: Param 7 in Delay 2 (p.4-12, p.4-15 7B). Param 6 is unused in this algorithm.

params.name: Diffusion
params.note: Param 8 in Delay 2 (p.4-12, p.4-16 7D).

params.name: Master Resonance
params.note: DECAY knob: average resonance 93-99.6% (p.4-21 13A, p.2-10); drives Master Resonance Feedback (6) to positive values only. Not in the p.4-12 table; MIDI resolution unpublished -- 16 = the knob's positions (see uncertain).

params.name: Fine Tuning
params.note: DELAY knob: tunes all 12 resonators -8..+7 semitones (lowest resonator normally 440 Hz); drives Tuning (9) (p.4-21 13B, p.2-10). p.2-7 instead says +-1 semitone in 1/8 steps. Not in the p.4-12 table; 16 = the knob's positions.

params.name: Pre-Delay (strum)
params.note: Spaces the onsets of the 6 resonator pairs (strum). Factory 130 ms. Table p.4-12: 256 steps; p.4-21 13C: 2730 steps.

params.name: Lo Freq Cut
params.note: High-pass on the input to tame boom on low tunings (p.4-21 13D).

params.name: Shimmer
params.note: Period of resonator detuning; factory one every 0.5 s (p.4-21 13E). 'Adjustable only via SysEx' (p.2-7).

params.name: Master Resonance Feedback
params.note: Resonance of the lowest resonator; the others follow via Slope. Never goes to zero (p.4-22 13F). Bipolar 64 steps.

params.name: Richness
params.note: Periodic detune depth; factory 1/3 semitone (p.4-22 13G).

params.name: Slope
params.note: Relative resonance of high vs low resonators (timbre). Table p.4-12 'Uni, 32 steps'; p.4-22 13H prints -15..+15, factory 10 -- shown as raw steps 0-31 because the step<->label mapping is not published.

params.name: Tuning
params.note: Tunes all twelve resonators over more than an octave in 1/8-semitone steps (p.4-22 13I). Driven by the DELAY knob via Fine Tuning (1).

params.name: Size (inverse length)
params.note: DECAY knob: perceived length of the inverse effect; changes size, so also timbre, and mutes while changing (p.4-17 10A, p.2-6). Shown 1-32.

params.name: Slope
params.note: Slope of the inverse build-up; normally maximum. Table p.4-13 says 32 steps, p.4-18 10B says 1-16, 16 steps -- see uncertain.

params.name: Pre-Delay
params.range: 0-262 ms via MIDI, 0-246 ms via knob
params.note: DELAY knob; param 8 in Inverse/Gate (p.4-16 7E).

params.name: Gate Time
params.note: DECAY knob: perceived gate length; actually changes size (and timbre), mutes while changing (p.4-17 9A, p.2-6).

params.name: Slope
params.note: Decay slope; normally maximum = flat (p.4-17 9B). Shown 1-16.

params.name: Pre-Delay
params.range: 0-262 ms via MIDI, 0-246 ms via knob
params.note: DELAY knob; param 8 in Inverse/Gate (p.4-16 7E).

params.name: Feedback
params.note: DECAY knob: positive feedback around the Delay 3 voice pair, 0-94%; drives Delay 3 Feedback (6) to positive values only (p.4-20 12A). Not in the p.4-13 table; 16 = the knob's positions (see uncertain).

params.name: Group Delay (Delay 1)
params.note: DELAY knob: base delay for all three voice pairs, exponential curve; MIDI sets finer values in 8.2 ms increments (p.4-20 12B, p.2-8). Delay 2/3 may add up to 1 s more as long as the total stays <= 1.6 s.

params.name: High Cut
params.note: Param 3 in Delay 1 (p.4-13, p.4-15 7B).

params.name: Delay 2 Spread
params.note: Adds up to 1 s to voice pair 2, linear (p.4-20 12C).

params.name: Delay 3 Spread
params.note: Adds up to 1 s to voice pair 3, linear (p.4-20 12C).

params.name: Delay 3 Feedback
params.note: Bipolar feedback around voice pair 3 (+-99% via SysEx, p.2-7).

params.name: Rate
params.note: Random chorusing rate (the voices wander +-4 ms, p.2-7). 16 steps; Hz not documented.

params.name: Patch 1 Source
params.note: MIDI patch source 0-127 (Table 1, p.4-9): 0-31 = CC 0-31, 32-63 = 'switches 0-31', 64 last note, 65 its velocity, 66 channel aftertouch, 67 pitch bend, 68 MIDI tempo. 69-127 undefined. Which CCs the 'switches' are, and how an empty patch is encoded, are not documented.

params.name: Patch 1 Destination
params.note: Microcode param number 0-9 (p.4-8, meaning per Program ID). 10 (Input Level) is offered by Opcode's editor ('input level, or any effect parameter') but the manual says 0-9 -- unverified.

params.name: Patch 1 Scale
params.note: Scale factor -127..+127, 8-bit two's complement (p.4-8, p.4-14); sent as a 16-bit param change with hi byte 0. offset = source x scale, added to the destination's base value. Panel learn: 12 o'clock = 0, one click = one destination step over the controller's full range (p.3-6).

params.name: Patch 2 Source
params.note: MIDI patch source 0-127 (Table 1, p.4-9): 0-31 = CC 0-31, 32-63 = 'switches 0-31', 64 last note, 65 its velocity, 66 channel aftertouch, 67 pitch bend, 68 MIDI tempo. 69-127 undefined. Which CCs the 'switches' are, and how an empty patch is encoded, are not documented.

params.name: Patch 2 Destination
params.note: Microcode param number 0-9 (p.4-8, meaning per Program ID). 10 (Input Level) is offered by Opcode's editor ('input level, or any effect parameter') but the manual says 0-9 -- unverified.

params.name: Patch 2 Scale
params.note: Scale factor -127..+127, 8-bit two's complement (p.4-8, p.4-14); sent as a 16-bit param change with hi byte 0. offset = source x scale, added to the destination's base value. Panel learn: 12 o'clock = 0, one click = one destination step over the controller's full range (p.3-6).

params.name: Processor Input Level
params.note: Param 10: 16-bit like the audio params but NOT stored in a register and reset to maximum on every setup recall (p.4-7). Not in any dump. Resolution undocumented, so the raw 14-bit offset above 0x8000 is shown (16383 = 0xBFFF = max). Not the front-panel INPUT pot (analogue).

params.name: Setup Number
params.note: Param 64 (8-bit, not stored): which setup runs. 0-127 = registers 0-127, 128-143 = presets 0-15 = Program knob positions 0-15 (p.4-7 prints '128-144'). Writing it loads that setup (the SysEx way to reach the ROM presets; PC only reaches registers). The unit TRANSMITS param 64 when the Program knob is turned (p.4-6). Which preset is knob position 0..15 is not documented: preset labels here follow the manual's program-table order and are provisional.

systemParams.name: Patch 1 offset
systemParams.note: 16-bit, = source x scale, recomputed continuously by the unit; writes are overwritten. Not stored. Read (62h/65h) to see what a patch adds (p.4-8).

systemParams.name: Program ID
systemParams.note: Also dump byte 0; modelled as params[programId].

1.name: Rooms & Halls
1.presets: Small 1/2, Medium 1/2, Large 1/2, Hall D, Hall B

algorithms.note: Each param in params[] carries algos[] = the Program IDs it exists in. Params 0-9 share wire numbers across algorithms with different meanings, so only the params whose algos include the current Program ID are live. 'unused' = param numbers the manual lists for no purpose in that algorithm (don't send).

leftToRight: SIGNAL PRESENT (green) + PEAK (red, -3 dB from overload) LEDs
Program selector: 16-position rotary, legends ROOM (Small 1/2, Medium 1/2, Large 1/2) | HALL D, B | PLATE D, B | EFFECT (Inverse, Gate, Chorus 1/2, Delay 1/2)
frontPanel.knobs: DECAY and DELAY have 16 positions and no end stop; the value wraps at 6 o'clock. After a program load the knob is not where the value is (the MIDI LED blinks) until it is moved, then it snaps (p.2-4). Their meaning per algorithm: algorithms[].params 0/1.
frontPanel.midiButton: Hold + send any complete channel message = learn the MIDI channel; hold + Program Change n = store the edit buffer into register n (LED flashes fast ~2 s); hold + move a MIDI controller then a DECAY/DELAY knob, set scale, release = Dynamic MIDI patch; hold + move a knob a couple of clicks (no controller) = delete that knob's patch (pp.3-2..3-7).
frontPanel.notMidi: INPUT, MIX and OUTPUT pots and the rear DEFEAT jack are analogue/not stored (p.3-3). No display: there is no way to see a register number or name on the unit.

banks.label: registers
banks.note: User registers 0-127 (battery-backed). PC n loads register n (p.3-3). Read without loading: 3n 61 <r> -> 1n <r> 38 <56> ck F7. Store: edit buffer -> 6n 70 <r> (event), or hold MIDI + PC r on the panel. Whether a received 1n stored dump writes the register is not stated. The front panel cannot select a register.

banks.label: presets
banks.note:
ROM presets 0-15 = setup numbers 128-143 = Program knob positions 0-15 (p.4-7). PC cannot reach them; select by writing param 64 = 128 + p (F0 06 02 2n 40 01

00 F7: b0 = 01 because bit 7 of 128 + p is set), then 3n 60 to read the edit buffer. Position-to-name order unverified (see uncertain).

programs.note: 128 registers + 16 presets + the edit buffer. No bank select. A register stores the Program ID, params 0-9, the 16-char name and 4 Dynamic MIDI patches; not input level (param 10), MIX/INPUT/OUTPUT or DEFEAT.

factoryPresetsNote: Program tables pp.2-9..2-10: each preset's DECAY/DELAY function, factory value and range. Halls/rooms/plates RT60 ranges differ per preset although they share Program IDs 1/2, so the presets also differ in hidden params (size, bass multiply, hi cut...).

factoryUserContents.note: Not documented. The manual never lists what ships in registers 0-127 (it warns that storing overwrites without checking, p.3-3). Read them with a 64h dump before writing anything.

ccMap.note: No fixed CC map. CCs act only through the 4 Dynamic MIDI patches stored per register (2 can be made on the panel by MIDI-learn, 2 more only by SysEx, p.3-4). Sources: CC 0-31, 32 switches, last note, velocity, aftertouch, pitch bend, MIDI tempo (Table 1, p.4-9). Destinations: params 0-9 of the running algorithm.

backup.restore: Send the 7176-byte 4n dump back (p.4-6: transmit and receive formats are identical) -- UNVERIFIED that the unit writes all registers from it; verify by re-reading 64h. Fallback per register: load the edit buffer (0n dump, or 2n param stream) then 6n 70 <r>, paced >= 30 ms. There is no write protect.
backup.notInSysex: MIDI channel (only by MIDI-button learn), the jumper, INPUT/MIX/OUTPUT pots, DEFEAT state.

setup: Open the unit and move the internal MIDI jumper from W3 (THRU, factory) to W2 (OUT): remove the two front-panel side screws, the nuts/washers on the DEFEAT, OUTPUTS and INPUTS jacks, slide the board out of the case, move the small (usually blue) jumper at the back of the board near the MIDI jacks onto the neighbouring pins (Opcode tech pub; service manual via monophreak). Without it the LXP-1 sends nothing and every read times out.
Cable both ways: interface out -> LXP-1 MIDI IN, LXP-1 MIDI OUT (the former THRU jack) -> interface in. The jack is then no longer a THRU: put the LXP-1 at the end of a chain.

MIDI channel (no OMNI, no display): hold the MIDI button, send any complete channel message on the editor's channel (a note or pitch bend; not under running status), release. SysEx carries the channel in byte 4 and must match.
Never hold the MIDI button while the editor sends a Program Change: MIDI + PC n stores the edit buffer into register n (and re-learns the channel).
Stores overwrite without warning (no write protect, no 'in use' check). Back up all 128 registers before the first write.
Leave the Program knob alone while editing: turning it loads a preset and discards edits (it also sends param 64). DECAY/DELAY knob moves overwrite whatever the editor sent to params 0/1.
INPUT / MIX / OUTPUT are analogue pots and are not in SysEx; set MIX full right (100% wet) when on a send.
If register contents come back as garbage, the memory battery may be dead.
uncertain: Sumcheck formula (sum vs negated sum, masked to 7 bits) and whether the byte-count byte(s) are included: the manual only says 'sum done on the bytes in packed format'. Learn it from the first dump.

Byte order of the 16-bit values inside the unpacked dump (lo-hi assumed from the parameter-message format and 'least significant data sent first', p.4-10). Verify: set DECAY knob to max, dump 60h, look at bytes 1-2 (expect BF xx or xx BF).

Step <-> 16-bit mapping. The manual gives steps over the 0x8000..0xBFFF (uni) / 0x4000..0xBFFF (bi) range but not how the unit quantises. Centre-of-bin values are sent; read-back rounding may differ. Raw 16-bit capture in the mapping session settles it.

Step counts that disagree inside the manual: Reverb Pre-Delay 8192 (p.4-11) vs '4096 steps, 2 samples each' (p.4-16); Flange Depth 256 (p.4-11) vs 124 x 6.25 us (p.4-18); Flange Rate 16 (p.4-11) vs 32 with a subdivided first step (p.4-19); Chorus 2 Pre-Delay 256 (p.4-12) vs 2730 (p.4-21); Inverse Slope 32 (p.4-13) vs 1-16 / 16 steps (p.4-18). The tables were used.
Hi Freq Cut in Rooms/Halls/Plates: table p.4-11 = param 4, Common Parameters p.4-15 = param 3 (which is Bass Multiply in the same table and on p.4-16). Param 4 used; confirm by ear.

Params with no MIDI resolution printed (not in the p.4-11..4-13 tables): Chorus 2 params 0/1 (Master Resonance, Fine Tuning) and Delay 1 param 0 (Feedback) -- modelled as 16 steps (the knob's resolution). They are macro params that drive 6 / 9 / 6 respectively. Chorus 2 Fine Tuning range: p.4-21 says -8..+7 semitones, p.2-7 says +-1 semitone in 1/8 steps.
Delay 2 Left/Right Delay (params 4/5) and Delay 1 Rate: time/Hz ranges not documented.

Preset order for setup numbers 128-143 / Program knob positions 0-15: not documented. Labels follow the program-table order (Small 1 .. Delay 2) and are provisional. Capture param 64 while turning the Program knob through all 16 positions.
p.4-7 prints presets as setups '128-144' (17 values for 16 presets): treated as 128-143.
Reply formats for 62h / 65h requests are inferred (2n / 5n messages), not printed. Event messages (6n) are listed as 'transmitted' on p.4-6 but no trigger for sending them is described.

Receiving dumps: whether a received 0n loads the edit buffer, a received 1n writes register p, and a received 4n rewrites all registers is not stated beyond 'identical in format' (p.4-6). Verify each before relying on it.
Event store/recall (70h/71h) have no acknowledgement; confirm with a 61h read-back.

Patch encoding details: 'no patch' value, which CC numbers the 32 'switches' are (CC 64-95 likely), whether destination 10 (Input Level, per Opcode) is valid, and which patch slots (1-2?) the front-panel learn uses.
Name character set and padding (16 x 8-bit, params 32-47).
Factory register contents (registers 0-127 as shipped) are not documented.
Pacing: no figure. Monophreak's LSP-1 editor notes loading needed a sleep to slow SysEx; 30 ms between messages used (PCM 70 family figure). A 7176-byte dump takes ~2.3 s on the wire.
Program ID as a writable param (65): p.4-7 says it 'controls which microcode algorithm is currently running', but whether writing it alone re-initialises params 0-9 is not stated.
Running status from the interface can break channel learn (p.3-2): send a note then a pitch bend if learning fails.
driverNotes: Lexicon LXP-1 (Lexicon 06h, model 02h). Every message is F0 06 02 <(type << 4) | n> ... F7, n = channel() (learned with the MIDI button; no OMNI, no device ID). Match incoming on F0 06 02 + type nibble; adopt the channel nibble if it differs. (1) DATA: a register/edit buffer is 49 unpacked bytes, sent 8/7-packed as 56 bytes (lexicon.formats.packing). unpack: for each 8-byte packet hdr,x0..x6: byte_i = x_i | ((hdr >> i) & 1) << 7. pack is the reverse. Layout = lexicon.dumpLayout; each param carries offset + size (2 for microcode, 1 for the rest). Microcode words: assume lo, hi (lexicon.formats.wordOrder) until verified. Value <-> wire: encoding 'lxp16uni' / 'lxp16bi' with p.steps (lexicon.encoding); 'twos8' for patch scales; plain bytes otherwise. Only params whose algos[] contains the dump's byte 0 are decoded/sent; keep the full 49-byte mirror so bytes for other params (and unused param slots) round-trip untouched. Sumcheck: learn the formula on the first dump (prefs 'sumcheck'), compute it for every dump sent. (2) READ: requestPatch = F0 06 02 3n 60 00 F7 -> F0 06 02 0n 38 <56> ck F7 (63 bytes), wait up to ~500 ms. requestProgram(0, r) = 3n 61 <r> -> 1n <r> 38 <56> ck F7 (64 bytes; match byte 5 = r). Presets cannot be dumped: select then requestPatch. (3) EDIT: sendParam(p, v) = F0 06 02 2n <p.pnum> <b0> <b1> <b2> F7 with w = wire(p, v): b0 = ((w >> 15) & 1) << 1 | ((w >> 7) & 1), b1 = w & 7F, b2 = (w >> 8) & 7F (lxpx). 8-bit params: w = v & FF. Coalesce per param, >= 30 ms apart. Don't send params not in the current algorithm. Size / Gate Time / Inverse Size mute the unit while changing: throttle (~150 ms). Program ID change: send 65 first, then re-read 60h (the unit may reset params). sendPatch(values) = until a received 0n is proven to load the edit buffer, stream Program ID, params 0-9 (current algorithm), name 32-47 and patches 48-59 as 2n messages. (4) programChange(0, r) = C0|n, r. Presets: 2n 40 <setup 128+p> (b0 = 01, b1 = p, b2 = 00); unverified. After any change, requestPatch. (5) writeProgram(0, r, values): sendPatch, wait ~100 ms, F0 06 02 6n 70 <r> F7, wait ~300 ms, verify with requestProgram(0, r). No ack, no write protect: the read-back is the confirmation. Never use LEARN/MIDI-button + PC from the editor. (6) probe: 3n 60 00 F7 on the saved channel, 400 ms; if silent sweep n = 0..15 (~150 ms each). No reply on any channel = jumper still at THRU (most likely) or OUT not cabled. (7) sameProgram(a, b): compare the 49 unpacked bytes, only the slots used by a's Program ID. (8) decode(ev): unsolicited 2n 00 / 2n 01 = DECAY / DELAY knob turned -> the current algorithm's pnum 0/1 param, value = base + patch offset; 2n 40 = Program knob (setup number) -> follow logic: re-read 60h. Also accept 5n nibble messages and unsolicited 0n/1n dumps (MRC or a slaved LXP-1). (9) PACING: 30 ms between short messages, >= 100 ms after a dump, one outstanding request. Bank backup: 3n 64 00 F7 -> 7176 bytes (~2.3 s; wait up to 5 s), split into 128 x 56 packed and unpack each; fallback 128 x 61h. (10) MAPPING SESSION (first time on the hardware): a) probe; dump 60h; learn the sumcheck; set DECAY knob min then max and diff the dumps (word order + raw 16-bit values per knob step); b) turn the Program knob through all 16 positions, log each 2n 40 value and the dump's Program ID, fix factoryPatchNames order; c) for each microcode param of one algorithm: send min / mid / max, read 60h, confirm the bytes and the centre-of-bin rounding, listen; d) 62h and 65h on param 0 -> log the reply formats; e) setup select: 2n 40 01 00 00 (setup 128) and 2n 40 01 0F 00 (setup 143); f) send a 1n dump to a scratch register (after a full 64h backup) and read it back; g) 6n 70 / 71 round trip; h) patch: MIDI-learn a CC on the panel, dump, decode which slot + source value + scale it wrote; i) only then try restoring a 4n dump. Record results in uncertain.
